fixer.summary:
The costed material check no longer hard-codes "holy symbol". Before, any spell with a material cost passed if the caster had a holy symbol. Now each spell's data names its component and a minimum price, and the cast is refused unless the caster carries that item worth at least that much.

Changes:
- **Spell data** (`dungdra/data/spells.py`): new `material_item` field. Bless sets it to "holy symbol"; `material_cost` stays at 5 GP.
- **Items** (`dungdra/items.py`): new `Item.unit_cost()`, which gives an item's value in copper. It uses a `cost` prop if the item has one, otherwise the equipment price table, the same way `unit_weight` works.
- **The check** (`dungdra/spells.py`, `_material`): looks through every item matching `material_item` and passes if any is worth at least `material_cost` GP. The refusal is the same as before, page 105, and it keeps the existing `SRD[SPELL.bless#4]` tag.

Three unit tests added:
- A made-up spell variant whose component is a 1,000 GP spyglass is refused without the spyglass and refused with only a holy symbol; it goes through once a spyglass is carried.
- A holy symbol worth only 4 GP is refused for Bless; one worth 5 GP is accepted.
- The Bless data names the holy symbol and the 5 GP price.

Results: `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` are clean, 276 unit tests pass, `dev-gate` passes, and the 75 spell/Bless/material acceptance and scenario tests pass. The ticket names no acceptance tests and `tests/` has no T-25 xfail marker, so there was nothing to run with `--runxfail`.

findings.explanation: test_bless_names_its_holy_symbol_and_price only reads the new data constants back (material_item == 'holy symbol', material_cost == 5). It checks no behaviour, and the two tests above it already cover the check. This is minor and doesn't block the change.

followups.title: gear.py (buy/sell valuation, lines ~147 and ~251) prices items with item_cost(name), so it ignores the new per-item `cost` prop that Item.unit_cost() honours. Route item valuation through Item.unit_cost() so one value mechanism exists

review.summary: I approve this fix. _material used to look up 'holy symbol' for every costed component. It now takes the item from the spell data (material_item), takes the minimum GP value from material_cost, and accepts any carried item of that kind worth at least that much. The value comes from Item.unit_cost(), a new method beside unit_weight(): a `cost` prop on the item wins, otherwise the equipment table's price is used. It sits in the right layers: the data says what the component is, items say what an item is worth, and spells applies the rule. Nothing is special-cased. The component-pouch/focus path for uncosted components is unchanged. Two of the new tests check real behaviour: a different item and price (spyglass, 1,000 GP) where a holy symbol is refused, and a holy symbol worth 4 GP refused while one worth 5 GP is accepted. The third test only reads constants back. Two minor caveats: a spell with material_cost but no material_item would crash in find_all(None), though today only Bless has a costed component; and find_all, unlike find, ignores an item's title.
